run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: Log evidence answers the customer's question. Across the four indices that exist for the pattern app-190-service-* (app-190-service-auth, -gateway, -inventory, -orders), trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR returns exactly six documents at 2026-11-21T04:47:00Z forming one ordered flow: gateway received POST /api/orders, auth authenticated user_12847, orders began processing SKU-78234 quantity 500, inventory then failed the stock reservation, orders reported that failure upward, and the gateway returned HTTP 400. The error originated at the inventory service's stock-reservation step: INV-ERR-4082, 'insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23' (duration 45 ms). orders then logged the propagated failure ORD-ERR-1001, and the gateway logged GW-ERR-400 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled', i.e. the error code returned to the caller was GW-ERR-400 / HTTP 400 Bad Request. The failure is isolated: across the full authorized 24-hour window only these three ERROR documents exist in app-190-service-*, and inventory logged 50 successful 'Stock reserved successfully' events around the failure; the message text itself indicates a stock shortfall rather than an infrastructure fault, so the exact reason the stock for SKU-78234 stood at 23 is not established. Jaeger and Prometheus were unavailable, so the flow is derived from correlated log documents, not from span parent-child references or metrics.

claims.text: Only four indices match app-190-service-*: app-190-service-auth (51 docs), app-190-service-gateway (52), app-190-service-inventory (51), app-190-service-orders (52). All four map trace_id, span_id, service, level, message, error_code, duration_ms and @timestamp.

A search for trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR across app-190-service-* returned six documents covering four services, all timestamped 2026-11-21T04:47:00.000Z to 04:47:00.140Z: gateway span-gw-err (INFO, 2 ms, 'Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847'), auth span-auth-err (INFO, 15 ms, 'User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token'), orders span-orders-err (INFO, 25 ms, 'Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500'), inventory span-inv-err (ERROR, 45 ms), orders span-orders-err-2 (ERROR, 130 ms, 'Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082'), gateway span-gw-err-2 (ERROR, 145 ms).

The earliest error in the trace is the inventory document: index app-190-service-inventory, service=inventory, span_id span-inv-err, level=ERROR, error_code=INV-ERR-4082, message 'Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23', duration_ms=45, timestamp 2026-11-21T04:47:00.080Z; the stock shortfall is the origin of the error chain (orders' and gateway's later errors only reference this failure).

The error code returned to the caller at the gateway was GW-ERR-400: index app-190-service-gateway, service=gateway, span_id span-gw-err-2, level=ERROR, error_code=GW-ERR-400, message 'Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled', duration_ms=145, timestamp 2026-11-21T04:47:00.140Z; this is the only ERROR/WARN document in the gateway index for the window.

The middle hop recorded ORD-ERR-1001: index app-190-service-orders, service=orders, span_id span-orders-err-2, level=ERROR, message 'Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082', duration_ms=130, timestamp 2026-11-21T04:47:00.130Z, i.e. orders propagated the inventory failure rather than originating it.

The failure is a single-request event, not a burst: over the whole authorized window (2026-11-20T05:14:00Z to 2026-11-21T05:14:00Z) app-190-service-* contains only three ERROR documents, all with trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR (INV-ERR-4082, ORD-ERR-1001, GW-ERR-400); the 04:14-05:14 slice shows 203 INFO vs 3 ERROR documents and each error_code appears exactly once.

Inventory was otherwise succeeding on the same code path: its index holds 51 documents in the window, 50 of them level=INFO 'Stock reserved successfully' at one per minute from 04:23:00.080Z through 05:12:00.080Z plus the single INV-ERR-4082 at 04:47:00.080Z.

orders logged the distinct message 'Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500' only for TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR; its other 50 order documents in the window are INFO 'Order created, checking inventory' and do not record a quantity, so no quantity baseline exists from these logs.

The Kubernetes cluster does not run inventory, orders or auth workloads: its 25 deployments are in app-102a (api-gateway, nginx:latest) and otel-demo/kube-system/local-path-storage, and its 33 pods contain no pod for inventory, orders or auth, so those services' only available telemetry is the shipped app-190-service-* log documents.

Rejected: an inventory infrastructure failure (timeout, crash, 5xx) caused the order failure. The inventory span completed in 45 ms, its error message states an explicit stock shortfall ('insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23'), and 50 other reservations succeeded in the same window; the evidence text rules out an availability/timeout explanation for this trace.

Rejected: orders or gateway originated the error. The orders document says 'inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082' and the gateway document only maps the outcome to '400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled'; both are downstream consequences of the inventory document, which is the earliest error in the trace.

The proximate cause is an order quantity (500 units of SKU-78234) exceeding available stock (23 units) in the inventory service's stock record at 04:47:00.080Z. Whether 500 units was an anomalous order, or the SKU-78234 stock figure itself was wrong or depleted, cannot be determined from available evidence: successful orders do not log quantities and no inventory master data or change history is readable here.

The gateway document records HTTP 400 / GW-ERR-400 (a client-side request rejection), not a 5xx server error, and gateway's 145 ms total duration is consistent with a fast, well-formed rejection rather than a timeout or retry storm.

gaps: Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services and Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query, so span parent-child references, span-level status, request rates and latency baselines could not be checked; the request flow above is reconstructed solely from log documents that share trace_id TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR and their timestamps.

No pod, Deployment or container for the inventory, orders or auth services exists in this cluster, so their pod status, restart/termination reasons, events and application stdout logs (including previous-container logs) could not be inspected.

Logs of the unrelated api-gateway pod (namespace app-102a, image nginx:latest) could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned POD_NOT_FOUND even though the pod appeared Running in the 05:14:08Z pod listing. That Deployment was scaled 0->1 with ReplicaSet api-gateway-585c5579f6 at 2026-11-21T05:13:08Z, after the 04:47 failure, and no evidence ties it to the app-190-service-gateway service; what caused that scale-up is unknown.

The reason the available stock for SKU-78234 was 23 and whether a 500-unit order is normal for this workload is not observable: the other orders documents carry no quantity, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

Whether any configuration, feature flag or deployment change affected the inventory service around 04:47:00Z could not be determined, because the inventory workload is not present in the cluster and change history is not integrated.
next_steps: Check inventory master data and replenishment records for SKU-78234 to confirm whether 23 units on hand at 2026-11-21T04:47:00Z was correct, and whether a 500-unit order for that SKU should have been accepted or rejected earlier in the flow.
Retry Jaeger and Prometheus when they are reachable to confirm the span graph for TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR and to verify that inventory error rate and latency were flat around the failure.
Confirm where the app-190 services actually run (they are not deployed in this cluster) so their pod status and application logs, including previous-container logs, can be inspected.
Review the api-gateway Deployment scale-up in namespace app-102a at 2026-11-21T05:13:08Z separately; it is unrelated to the 04:47 order failure on the evidence seen.
